questions.question: In a chemical reaction between sulphuric acid and barium chloride solution the white precipitates formed are of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barium sulfate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **On reaction with the sulphuric acid solution, barium chloride forms a white precipitate of barium sulfate.**

 
 
• **BaCl2​+H2​SO4​→BaSO4​+2HCl**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Double displacement reactions may be defined as the chemical reactions in which one component of each of both the reacting molecules is exchanged to form the products**. 

 
 
• ​​During this reaction, the cations and anions of two different compounds switch places, forming two entirely different compounds**.**
 
 
 
• **Double displacement reactions generally take place in aqueous solutions in which the ions precipitate and there is an exchange of ions.**
 
• For example, on mixing a solution of barium chloride with sodium sulfate, a white precipitate of barium sulfate is immediately formed. These reactions are ionic in nature.
 
 
• The reactants change into ions when dissolved in water and there is an exchange of ions in solution. This results in the formation of a product molecule.
 
 
 
• **Double displacement reactions can be further classified as neutralization, precipitation, and gas formation reactions.**
 
• **Neutralization reactions** are a specific kind of double displacement reaction. An acid-base reaction occurs when an acid reacts with an equal quantity of base. The acid-base reaction results in the formation of salt (neutral in nature) and water.
 
• ** HCI(aq)+NaOH(aq) longrightarrow NaCI(aq)+H₂O(I)**
 
• **Precipitation **is the formation of a solid in a solution or inside another solid during a chemical reaction**. **
 
 
• **​**This process usually takes place when the concentration of dissolved ions in the solution exceeds the solubility product. 
 
 
 
• **A double displacement reaction should also occur if an insoluble gas is formed**. Gases such as HCl and NH3 are soluble in water, but some other gases, such as H2S, are not soluble in water.

questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is not completely curable?
questions.solution:
**__Concept__**: 

__
 
• When a disease is transmitted from an infected person to an uninfected one through sexual contact, it is termed a sexually transmitted disease.
 
• The causative agent of STDs can be a bacterium, virus or another parasite.
 
• Examples - genital herpes, human papillomavirus, gonorrhoea etc.

**Explanation__****:**

**Option 1: **Gonorrhoea – **INCORRECT**

 
• Gonorrhoea is caused by a bacterium and it is possible to cure gonorrhoea.
 
• The Centre for Disease Control recommends intramuscular ceftriaxone for the treatment of this disease
 
• Hence, this option is incorrect.

Option 2: Genital warts– INCORRECT

 
• Genital warts are caused by HPV and can be removed surgically.
 
• Hence, this option is incorrect.

Option 3: Genital herpes – CORRECT

 
• Genital herpes is caused by herpes simplex virus type II.
 
• Till today, there is no cure for the type-II-herpes simplex virus
 
• Hence, this option is correct.

Option 4: Chlamydiosis – INCORRECT

 
• Chlamydiosis is a bacterial disease.
 
• Azithromycin is used for its treatment.
 
• Hence, this option is incorrect.

So, the correct answer is** option 3).**

questions.concept: Conservation of Mechanical Energy, Work  Power Energy
questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct ?

**Statement 1: **In a closed system where non-conservative forces are present, the mechanical energy of the system is not conserved.

**Statement 2: **The principle of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, but it can be transformed from one form to another.

options.text: None of the statements are correct.

questions.solution:
The correct statement is__** option (3)**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• in a closed system where non-conservative forces (like friction or air resistance) are present, the mechanical energy of the system is not conserved. Non-conservative forces do work on the system that changes the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential energy).**this statement is correct.**
 
• The principle of conservation of energy, also known as the first law of thermodynamics, states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, but it can be transformed from one form to another. This means the total energy in a closed system remains constant. It can change from potential to kinetic energy, or to other forms like thermal energy, but the total amount of energy remains constant.** this statement is also correct.**
 
• **In a closed system (a system that does not interact with its surroundings),** the mechanical energy is usually conserved.
 
• **when non-conservative forces like friction or air resistance** are present, they do work on the system that changes the** total mechanical energy.** This means **the mechanical energy of the system is not conserved.**
 
• The **principle of conservation of energy** states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, but it can be transformed from one form to another.
 
• This statement is known as the **first law of thermodynamics **or the principle of conservation of energy. It states that the total amount of energy in a closed system remains constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Friction**: Friction is a non-conservative force that converts mechanical energy into heat. This is observed when you rub your hands together.
 
• **Air Resistance:** Air resistance is a non-conservative force that can slow down a moving object, converting its kinetic energy into thermal energy.
 
• **Tension in a Cord:** Tension is a non-conservative force that can do work on an object, changing its kinetic energy.
 
• **Light Bulbs**: When an electrical connection is established, the electrical energy gets converted into light energy.
 
• **Collision**: A moving object induces motion into a stationary object after hitting it. The kinetic energy of the moving object is transferred to the stationary object.
 
• **Falling Objects**: An object at a certain height possesses potential energy. When it falls, the potential energy gets converted into kinetic energy.
 
• **Burning Woods**: The potential energy in wood is converted into heat and light energy when it burns.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question:
Match the following :

 
 

 Oxide
 Nature
 
 

 (a)
 CO
 (i)
 Basic
 
 

 (b)
 BaO
 (ii)
 Neutral
 
 

 (c)
 Al₂O₃
 (iii)
 Acidic
 
 

 (d)
 Cl₂O₇
 (iv)
 Amphoteric
 
 

Which of the following is **correct** option?
questions.solution:
**Concept -**

__Nature of oxides__ -

Generally, metals form basic oxides because they can donate electrons and non-metals form acidic oxides because they can accept electrons. The basic nature of oxides increases down the group and decreases along a period, for ex - MgO, CaO, etc.

Amphoteric oxides are those which behave as both acidic and basic oxides. They can react with acid as well as the base. For example - BeO, Al₂O₃, etc.

Neutral oxides are neither acidic nor basic. For example - H₂O, N₂O, CO, etc.

__**Explanation -**__

Step 1 - Find out the metal oxides in the given table, they are basic in nature.

Step 2 - Find out non-metal oxides, they are acidic.

Step 3 - Find out the oxides are neither acidic nor basic, they are neutral in nature.

Step 4 - Find the amphoteric oxides that can react with both acid as well as base.

Step 5 - Match them accordingly.

Out of the given oxides,

Barium is alkaline earth metal. Hence, oxides of it are basic in nature.

So, **BaO = Basic oxide**

Chlorine is a halogen (non-metal) and can easily accept an electron. Its oxide is acidic in nature.

So, **Cl₂O₇ = Acidic oxide **

CO neither reacts with acid nor with base. Its oxides are neutral in nature.

So, **CO = Neutral oxide **

Al can react with both acid as well as base. Its oxides are amphoteric in nature.

So, **Al₂O₃ = Amphoteric oxide**

Now match them accordingly,

(a) CO - (ii) Neutral oxide

(b) BaO - (i) Basic oxide

(c) Al₂O₃ - (iv) Amphoteric oxide

(d) Cl₂O₇ - (iii) Acidic oxide

**Hence, our answer is to be, (a) - (ii), (b) - (i). (c) - (iv), (d) - (iii).**

The correct answer is option **4**.

questions.question: Which part of the brain extends to form the spinal cord?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Note **->

__
 
• Brain stem has -> Diencephalon, Midbrain, Pons, and Medulla oblongata
 
• Medulla along with brain stem continues to form Spinal cord.

**About Brain **->

 
• The **brain** is the **central information processing organ** of our body, and acts as the ‘command and control system’.
 
• It controls the voluntary movements, the balance of the body, the functioning of vital involuntary organs (e.g., lungs, heart, kidneys, etc.), thermoregulation, hunger and thirst, circadian (24-hour) rhythms of our body, activities of several endocrine glands and human behaviour.
 
• It is also the site for the processing of vision, hearing, speech, memory, intelligence, emotions, and thoughts.
 
• The brain can be divided into **three major parts**: (i) forebrain, (ii) midbrain, and (iii) hindbrain.
 
• The **spinal cord is a cable of neurons extending from the brain**.
 
• It is enclosed and protected by the vertebral column (spine) and layers of membranes known as meninges.
 
• The spinal cord carries information to and from the brain and produces basic patterns of locomotion.
 
• It can also act independently of the brain as part of the simple nerve circuits that produce reflexes i.e., the body’s automatic responses to certain stimuli. 

**Explanation**__:

__
 
• The part of the brain which extends to form the spinal cord is the **medulla oblongata**.
 
• Medulla is a **part of the hindbrain** and is connected to the midbrain by the pons.
 
• It forms a part of the brainstem that connects the spinal cord to the brain.
 
• It controls autonomic functions like **heartbeat and respiration**.
 
• It also controls other activities like** swallowing, digestion and vomiting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc7573d6db1d2a39ab2ceb4f3c7fcebc4b667460c86dac3cff3d8d3d37b43ec3.png] 

**Additional Information**:__

 
• **Cerebrum** -

 
 
• It is the largest part of the brain in humans which is organized into the left and right cerebral hemispheres and has many fissures and folds.
 
• It acts as an integrating center for emotions, memory, learning and other highly complex functions of the CNS.
 
 
 
• **Cerebellum** -
 
 
• It is the region of the human brain that lies above the medulla (brainstem) and behind the forebrain.
 
• It is responsible for integrating sensory inputs on the positions of joints and muscles, along with auditory and visual information, to coordinate body movements.
 
 
 
• **Hippocampus** -
 
 
• It is a complex brain structure located deep in the temporal lobe and plays a significant role in learning and memory.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are ***correctly*** matched pairs concerning Newton's Law of Motion?

1. First Law of Motion: Every body continues to be in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled by some external force to act otherwise.

2. Second Law of Motion: To every action, there is always an equal and opposite reaction. 

3. Third Law of Motion: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction in which the force acts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 only.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Newton's First Law of Motion**

 
• **Every body continues to be in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled by some external force to act **otherwise. Hence, **Statement 1 is correct.**
 
• The **state of rest or uniform linear motion **both implies** zero acceleration.**
 
• The** first law of motion** can, therefore, be simply expressed as:** If the net external force on a body is zero, its acceleration is zero. **
 
• **Acceleration **can be **non-zero** only if there is a **net external force on the body**.
 
• The **first law refers to the simple case **when the **net external force on a body is zero.**

**Newton's Second Law of Motion**

 
• The second law of motion refers to the **general situation when there is a net external force acting on the body.**
 
• The **momentum **of a **body **is defined to be the **product of its mass m and velocity v** and is denoted by **p: [p = mv] ** 
 
• **Momentum is clearly a vector quantity. **
 
• The **same force** for the same time **causes** the **same change in momentum for different bodies.**
 
• The **rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force **and **takes place in the direction in which the force **acts. Hence, **Statement 3 is incorrect.**

**Newton's Third Law of Motion**

 
• To every action,** there is always an equal and opposite reaction.** Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• There is **no cause-effect relation implied in the third law. **
 
• Consider a pair of bodies **A and B. According to the third law, FAB = – FBA [(force on A by B) = – (force on B by A)]**

• ** Bromoethanes:**

• **Chloroform:**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about diffusion?

options.text: The rate of diffusion remains constant on decreasing the temperature of the diffusing substance
The rate of diffusion increases on decreasing the temperature of the diffusing substance
The rate of diffusion increases on increasing the temperature of the diffusing substance
The rate of diffusion decreases on increasing the temperature of the diffusing substance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **3 **i.e. __**The rate of diffusion increases on increasing with the temperature of the diffusing substance.**__

 
• **Details about the process of Diffusion:**

 
 
• The spreading out and mixing of a substance with another substance due to the **motion of its particles **is called **diffusion.**
 
• It is a property of matter which is based on the **motion of its articles**.
 
• It is the **fastest in gases** and **slowest in solids**.
 
• The rate of diffusion **increase in increasing the temperature** of the diffusing substance.
 
• The phenomenon of diffusion tells us about the particles of matter that are** constantly moving**.
 
• **Light gases** diffuse** faster **than the **heavy gases** in the environment.
 
 
 
• There are **few examples** of diffusion mentioned below for better understanding:
 
 
• The **smell of food** being cooked reaches us even from a considerable distance by the process of diffusion only.
 
• The **fragrance of the burning incense sticks** spreads all around due to the diffusion of its smoke into the air.
 
• The **smell of perfume** spreads due to the diffusion of perfume vapors into the air.

questions.question: What determines the chemical properties of a carbon compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Functional group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The functional group in a carbon compound is primarily responsible for its chemical properties.
 
• Functional groups are specific groups of atoms within molecules that have their own characteristic properties, regardless of the other atoms present in a molecule.
 
• Examples of functional groups include hydroxyl groups (-OH), carboxyl groups (-COOH), and amino groups (-NH₂).
 
• The reactivity of a carbon compound can be significantly altered by the presence of different functional groups.
 
• Functional groups are key determinants in the chemical reactions that a molecule can undergo.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Mass**

 
 
• Molecular mass is the sum of the masses of all the atoms in a molecule.
 
• It influences the physical properties of a substance, such as boiling and melting points, but not the chemical properties directly.
 
 
 
• **Number of Hydrogen Atoms**
 
 
• The number of hydrogen atoms in a carbon compound can affect its saturation level, but is not a primary determinant of its chemical properties.
 
 
 
• **Length of the Carbon Chain**
 
 
• The length of the carbon chain can influence the physical properties of the compound, such as solubility and boiling point, but the functional group is more critical in determining chemical reactivity.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are false?

A. The value of G on the Moon is the same as its value on Earth.

B. The force of gravity between the centres of two masses of 2kg placed at a distance of 1m is 26.68 × 10-11 N.

C. Gravitational Force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between two objects.

D. The gravitational force between two objects doubles when the distance between them is halved.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gravity:**

 
 
• The acceleration due to gravity is the rate of increase of velocity of a body falling freely towards the earth.
 
• It is represented by: g= {GM_e over R_e²}
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Force:**

 
 
• Mathematically, it is represented as: 
 
• F= {GMmover r²}
 
• Where,
 
 
• F is the gravitational force
 
• G is gravitational constant
 
• M is the mass of the first particle
 
• m is the mass of the second particle
 
• r is the distance between them.
 
 
 
• Substituting G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹, m₁ = 2 kg, m₂ = 2 kg, and r = 1 m, the force comes out to 26.68 × 10⁻¹¹ N.
 
• This is called** Newton’s universal law of gravitation.**
 
• The **value of G is 6.67 × 10****⁻¹¹**** N m****²****/kg****²****.**
 
• The value of g on the Moon is 1/6th of that on the earth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• **"g" is the Gravitational acceleration** but **"G" is the Gravitational constant.**

 
 
• **​g can vary from place to place;** on **Moon, it is 1.62 m/s², but on earth, it is 9.807 m/s²**
 
• **​But G remains constant.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Thomson's model of an atom is INCORRECT?

options.text: The negative and positive charges are not equal in magnitude. So, the atom as a whole is not electrically neutral.
The positive charge in the atom is spread all over like the red edible part of a watermelon, while the electrons are studded in the positively charged sphere, like the seeds in the watermelon.
The negative and positive charges are equal in magnitude. So, the atom as a whole is electrically neutral.
An atom consists of a positively charged sphere and the electrons are embedded in it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thomson's model proposed that the atom is electrically neutral overall, with the positive and negative charges being equal in magnitude.
 
• The model suggested that the positive charge is uniformly spread throughout the atom, similar to the red edible part of a watermelon.
 
• Electrons were thought to be embedded within this positively charged sphere, akin to seeds in a watermelon.
 
• Thomson's model did not account for the nucleus; it assumed the atom was a single continuous positively charged entity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **J.J. Thomson:** An English physicist who is credited with the discovery of the electron in 1897, which led to the development of his atomic model.
 
• **Plum Pudding Model:** Thomson's atomic model is also known as the "plum pudding model" where electrons are like plums embedded in a positively charged "pudding."
 
• **Limitations of Thomson's Model:** The model was later refuted by Rutherford's gold foil experiment, which demonstrated the existence of a small, dense nucleus.
 
• **Rutherford's Model:** Introduced in 1911, it proposed that the atom consists of a dense nucleus surrounded by electrons, which provided a more accurate representation of atomic structure.
 
• **Electron:** A subatomic particle with a negative charge, discovered by J.J. Thomson, fundamental to the structure of atoms and chemistry.

questions.question: The breakdown of glucose in cytoplasm results in the formation of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pyruvate and energy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Glycolysis:**

 
• Glycolysis is the process in which** glucose is broken down to produce energy.**
 
• **It produces two molecules of pyruvate, ATP, NADH, and water.**
 
• The process** takes place in the cytoplasm of a cell and does not require oxygen.**
 
• It occurs in both aerobic and anaerobic organisms.
 
• Glycolysis is the primary step of cellular respiration, which occurs in all organisms.
 
• The process** takes place in the cytoplasm of **both **plant and animal cells.**
 
• **Six enzymes are involved **in the process.
 
• Glycolysis is followed by the Krebs cycle during aerobic respiration.
 
• In the absence of oxygen, the cells make small amounts of ATP as glycolysis is followed by fermentation.
